_readme: GAME CONTENT, DRAFT PENDING PRODUCER REVIEW (every Name, Title, Text, Intro and BondText). The discovery layer (docs/design/kinship-discovery.md): per region, 1 fog over each stage map and MinPois-MaxPois points of interest per stage (Kinship sites included), laid out by BeastCraft.Discovery.PoiLayout from the region's own discovery seed (RegionProgress.DiscoverySeed, never the map seed, so a replay never moves them), off the node map (never a MapNodeType: the pacing simulator never routes them). Kinds: Shrine (records a discovery and grants its GroveUnlockId, held for the Grove), LoreStone (the region's Lore entries that are no Kinship site's own, dealt in file order), Cache (the region's Caches that are no site's fallback, dealt in file order: fixed gold, materials and looks, never rolled), Vista (lifts a large chunk of fog; at most one a stage), KinshipSite (authored: a trial, TemplateId, at its map row's level + LevelOffset; its win offers two not-yet-owned beasts, Preferred first then roster order; the choice joins at the fielded team's mean level - 3, at least 1; BondCondition is flavour only: stance:{Stance}, element:{Element}, no_knockout or ''; a site with nothing left to offer grants its own LoreId and FallbackCacheId instead). Weights draw the non-Kinship kinds. A region's 100% (every map row of every stage walked and every point found) grants CompletionLook (a cosmetic-library discovery look) and CompletionGold. Rewards are non-combat or existing economy only. Validated by BeastCraft.Discovery.DiscoveryLibraryValidator (content load and the EditMode tests).

KinshipSites.Name: Mossbound Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win with a Vanguard holding the line.
KinshipSites.Intro: Wild beasts watch from the moss around the old stone. Show them how your team stands together, and one may choose to walk with you.

KinshipSites.Name: Cinderglow Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win without a beast being knocked out.
KinshipSites.Intro: The stone glows like a coal as you come near. Something bright is watching from the ash, waiting to see what kind of team you are.

KinshipSites.Name: Tidewrack Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win with a Ranged beast in the team.
KinshipSites.Intro: The tide has just let the stone go. Something patient stirs in the pool beside it, curious about you.

KinshipSites.Name: Galecrest Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win with a Skirmisher darting round the side.
KinshipSites.Intro: The wind howls everywhere but here. On the still stone, a pair of bright eyes is weighing you up.

KinshipSites.Name: Ironroot Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win without a beast being knocked out.
KinshipSites.Intro: Iron roots hold the stone like a hand. Something heavy and stubborn is dozing against it, one eye open.

KinshipSites.Name: Rimeglass Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win with a Vanguard holding the line.
KinshipSites.Intro: The stone is clear as ice. Look into it and a beast looks back, then steps out of the snow to meet you.

KinshipSites.Name: Deepshade Stone
KinshipSites.BondText: Bond: win without a beast being knocked out.
KinshipSites.Intro: A dark stone drinks the snowlight. In its shadow, something sly and quiet has been waiting a long time for a friend.

Lore.Title: The First Binders
Lore.Text: Moss has grown over the carving, but the shape is plain: a person and a beast side by side, each with a hand or a paw on the same stone. The first Beastbinders asked. They never commanded.

Lore.Title: Firefly Road
Lore.Text: Travellers once lit this path with jars of fireflies. The jars are long gone, but on warm nights the fireflies still come, as if they remember the way.

Lore.Title: The Warden Oath
Lore.Text: Worn words under a mossy arch: "Keep the Seal, keep the peace." The Gloam has left the Warden keeping the first half and forgetting the second.

Lore.Title: Humming Stones
Lore.Text: Press an ear to the standing stones and you can hear them hum. The old songs say they hum louder whenever a beast and a binder trust each other nearby.

Lore.Title: The Ash Gardens
Lore.Text: Nothing should grow on these ridges, yet red flowers push up through the ash each spring. Villagers call them hearthbuds and leave one on every doorstep for luck.

Lore.Title: The Twin Flames
Lore.Text: Two sparks, the story goes, leapt from the peak on the same night and never once burned apart. The Ember Twins still guard their Seal together, though the Gloam has made them forget why.

Lore.Title: Kiln Road
Lore.Text: Potters once carried their clay up here to fire it in the mountain breath. Shards of glazed cups still glitter in the path, bright as beetle wings.

Lore.Title: Cinder Sky
Lore.Text: At dusk the rocks glow and the sky turns the colour of a banked fire. Old travellers said the mountain was dreaming, and walked softly so as not to wake it.

Lore.Title: Drowned Bells
Lore.Text: When the tide pours in, the bells of the sunken towers ring beneath the water. Divers say the sound is sweet, not sad: the towers were built to be drowned twice a day.

Lore.Title: The Colossus Wakes
Lore.Text: The Colossus sat so long in the deepest pool that shellfish grew on its shoulders. The Gloam woke it, and it has been muddled and grumpy ever since.

Lore.Title: Brine Charts
Lore.Text: Scratched into the cave wall: a map of the currents, marked with little leaping fish. Whoever drew it knew the tides as well as their own heartbeat.

Lore.Title: The Frost Current
Lore.Text: A cold stream runs in from the north and frosts the deepest pools. The creatures of Tidefall follow it like a road home.

Lore.Title: Rope Bridges
Lore.Text: Every bridge here was tied by hand, knot by knot, by crag folk who sang to keep the rhythm. The wind still plucks them like harp strings.

Lore.Title: The Nesting Cliffs
Lore.Text: Griffins and thunderbirds share these cliffs the old way: griffins by day, thunderbirds by storm. Neither ever takes the other ledge.

Lore.Title: The Gale Titan
Lore.Text: The Titan once turned the winds so the crag folk could harvest. Now the Gloam makes it blow without stopping, and it cannot remember how to be still.

Lore.Title: Above the Clouds
Lore.Text: Up here the clouds are the ground and the sky goes on forever. A binder journal, pinned under a stone: "Came to see the view. Stayed for the company."

Lore.Title: Storm Eggs
Lore.Text: Thunderbird eggs crackle softly in their nests, and the crag folk hum to them through every storm. A calm egg, they say, hatches a steady flyer.

Lore.Title: The Lost Kite
Lore.Text: A child kite is tangled high on the crag, its tail snapping in the wind. Every traveller who passes adds a knot to keep it from blowing away.

Lore.Title: The Bell Trees
Lore.Text: The iron trees ring when the wind moves them, each with its own note. A lost traveller can find the way out by following the lowest bells.

Lore.Title: The Iron Stags
Lore.Text: The stags grow new antlers of ore every year and shed the old ones in the rain. Smiths once gathered them politely, leaving copper coins in thanks.

Lore.Title: Red Rain
Lore.Text: When it rains in Rustwood the puddles run red and the air smells of pennies. The creatures love it: they roll in the rust like cats in sunshine.

Lore.Title: Ore Seams
Lore.Text: Bright seams of copper wind through the stones like threads of light. Tarasques guard the richest ones, not out of greed, but because they like to sleep on them.

Lore.Title: Copper Path
Lore.Text: Someone laid copper coins along the forest floor, one every few steps. Follow them and they lead, in a long slow loop, right back to where you started.

Lore.Title: The Quiet Forge
Lore.Text: An old forge stands cold among the iron trees. On rainy days the trees ring the very notes the hammers once made.

Lore.Title: The Singing Ice
Lore.Text: At night the frozen lake groans and chimes as it settles. The snow folk say it is the lake singing to whatever sleeps beneath it.

Lore.Title: The Matriarch
Lore.Text: The Frost Matriarch has watched over the lake for longer than anyone can count. The Gloam has made her fierce, but her young still gather at her feet.

Lore.Title: Pine Lanterns
Lore.Text: Lanterns hang in the snowfield pines to guide travellers home. Someone still lights them each evening, though no one ever sees who.

Lore.Title: Beneath the Lake
Lore.Text: Deep under the ice something vast turns in its sleep, and the whole lake shivers. The old maps mark the spot with a single word: hush.

Lore.Title: Ice Skaters
Lore.Text: Snow folk children race across the frozen lake on bone skates, and the young frost wyrms race right beside them, grinning.

Lore.Title: The Last Light
Lore.Text: On the longest night the lake glows faintly from below, as if the sleeper beneath it has lit a lamp to read by.

Lore.Title: Mossbound Stone
Lore.Text: Beasts of the Hollow come to this stone to decide who they will walk beside. It is soft with moss and warm to the touch, even at night.

Lore.Title: Cinderglow Stone
Lore.Text: A stone as warm as bread from the oven. Beasts that bond here say its heat is the mountain blessing a good friendship.

Lore.Title: Tidewrack Stone
Lore.Text: Twice a day the sea covers this stone and twice a day it lets it go. Beasts that choose a binder here are patient ones: they have learned to wait for the tide.

Lore.Title: Galecrest Stone
Lore.Text: The wind never touches this stone, however hard it blows around it. Beasts that meet their binder here say the calm was waiting just for them.

Lore.Title: Ironroot Stone
Lore.Text: Roots of iron have grown right around this stone and hold it like a hand. Bonds made here are said to be as hard to break as the roots themselves.

Lore.Title: Rimeglass Stone
Lore.Text: This stone is clear as glass and cold as the lake. Look into it and you see the beast who will choose you, looking back.

Lore.Title: Deepshade Stone
Lore.Text: A dark stone that drinks the snowlight. Beasts of shadow bond here in the long evenings, when the lake is quietest.

Shrines.Name: Glade Shrine
Shrines.Text: A little shrine of stacked stones, fresh flowers at its foot. Something of this glade will grow in your Grove one day.

Shrines.Name: Firefly Shrine
Shrines.Text: Fireflies drift around a tiny lantern shrine. You take one glowing seed of the idea home with you.

Shrines.Name: Ember Shrine
Shrines.Text: A brazier that has never gone out, tended by no one. Its warmth follows you a little way down the path.

Shrines.Name: Hearthbud Shrine
Shrines.Text: Red hearthbuds bloom around a stone bowl of ash. One seed rolls into your hand as if it wanted to come.

Shrines.Name: Tidepool Shrine
Shrines.Text: A ring of shells around a still, clear pool. You could swear the water remembers your face.

Shrines.Name: Driftwood Shrine
Shrines.Text: An arch of pale driftwood, smoothed by a hundred tides. The sea hums through it softly.

Shrines.Name: Chime Shrine
Shrines.Text: Chimes of bone and glass sing in the endless wind. Their tune stays in your head all day.

Shrines.Name: Thistle Shrine
Shrines.Text: Thistles with heads like little clouds nod around a cairn. One puff drifts after you.

Shrines.Name: Bell Shrine
Shrines.Text: An iron bell hangs from a rusted branch. It rings once as you pass, low and friendly.

Shrines.Name: Copper Shrine
Shrines.Text: A sapling with copper leaves grows from a crack in the shrine stone. You pocket a single bright seed.

Shrines.Name: Snow Shrine
Shrines.Text: A quiet hollow in the snow, sheltered and still. It feels like a place a beast would love to nap.

Shrines.Name: Lantern Shrine
Shrines.Text: A lantern carved from clear ice, glowing without a flame. You carry the shape of it home in your mind.
